Opposite Party/s
 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Nilendu Kumar Choudhary, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party/s : Mr. Jitendra Kumar Singh, App
Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice S. B. Pd. Singh
Oral Order
2 05-12-2025 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.

2. The instant application for anticipatory bail has been filed by the petitioner apprehending his arrest in a case instituted for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 471, 504, 506 and 34 of the IPC and Section 67 of the I.T. Act.
Later on Sections 354(D) and 509 of the IPC was also added.

3. The prosecution case is that Jyoti Kumari, a Maithili folk singer, submitted a written complaint to the Officer-in-Charge of the Cyber Police Station, Darbhanga, alleging that for the last 15 days, a Facebook ID named "Krishna Paidist" has been abusing, threatening, and posting objectionable comments against her with an intent to defame her.

She further stated that about five months earlier, one Patna High Court CR. MISC. No. 84189 of 2025(2) dt.05-12-2025 Vidyanand Chaupal (petitioner), an event conductor with whom she had previously worked, had demanded illicit physical favours, after which she stopped working with him.
However, he continued to follow her and she suspects that the abusive posts and comments are being made by him through the said Facebook ID.
4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence.

It is stated that from perusal of the FIR it appears that the petitioner is an event manager for whom the informant used to work, and there existed a dispute between them regarding payment for various events.
The informant had even threatened to implicate the petitioner in false cases and in the background of such dispute, the present FIR has been lodged out of such grudge.

It is further submitted that the parties have amicably settled the dispute, and a compromise petition has been filed, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexure-P/2 to this Vidyanand Chaupal vs The State Of Bihar on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37433565/
1 petition.

entities.text: Vidyanand Chaupal vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner claims clean antecedent.
5. Learned A.P.P. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer of bail.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the case as stated above, this Patna High Court CR. MISC. No. 84189 of 2025(2) dt.05-12-2025 Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

The petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court below within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt/production of this order and in the event of his arrest or surrender in connection with Cyber P.S. Case no. 74 of 2023, they will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Darbhanga subject to the conditions as laid down under section 482 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

(S. B. Pd. Singh, J) AjayMishra/-
